extracted.intended_audience: authors, illustrators, publishers, and librarians preparing or submitting children's and young adult books for consideration for the Pura Belpré Award; and committee members administering the award
extracted.subtask_short: Pura Belpré Award eligibility and criteria
extracted.subtask_description: Terms, definitions, textual and illustrative evaluation criteria, and submission procedures for the Pura Belpré Award, which recognizes outstanding portrayal of the Latino cultural experience in children's and young adult literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award purpose / central evaluative requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Pura Belpré Award is presented to a Latino/Latina writer and illustrator whose work best portrays, affirms, and celebrates the Latino cultural experience in an outstanding work of literature for children and youth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The committee should evaluate how the work portrays, affirms, and celebrates Latino cultural experience; particular attention will be paid to cultural authenticity. The award is for both literary/illustrative quality and presentation for children.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award categories and frequency
rubrics_metrics.description: Three medals shall be awarded annually: one to a Latino author of an outstanding children’s book, one to a Latino author of an outstanding young adult book, and one to a Latino illustrator for creating an outstanding children’s picture book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each medal must be an original work that portrays, affirms and celebrates the Latino cultural experience. Honor books may be named. If suitable candidates are not found, the awards will not be presented in that year. (Note: the Young Adult Author category was added beginning with the 2021 award.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication location and timing eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The award-winning books must be published in the United States or Puerto Rico during the preceding year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: “Published in the preceding year” means the book has a publication date in the year under consideration, was available for purchase in that year, and has a copyright date no later than that year. An eligible book may have a copyright date prior to the year under consideration if it was not published until the year under consideration. Books originally published in other countries are not eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient residency/citizenship requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients of the Pura Belpré medal must be residents or citizens of the United States or Puerto Rico.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: “Resident” specifies that the author has established and maintained residence in the United States, or Puerto Rico, as distinct from being a casual or occasional visitor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language and format eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Fiction and nonfiction books for children published in Spanish, English, or bilingual formats are eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A “children’s book” is a book for which children are an intended potential audience (children defined as ages up to and including 14). A “children’s picture book” is one that essentially provides the child with a visual experience and has a collective unity of story line, theme, or concept developed through the series of pictures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original work / reprints and compilations
rubrics_metrics.description: Each of the award-winning books must be an original work. Reprints and compilations are not eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In defining “original work,” the committee may consider books that are traditional in origin if the book is the result of original research and the retelling and interpretation are the writer’s own.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author / illustrator heritage and co-creator rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Author may include co-authors; illustrator may include co-illustrators. In the case where a co-author or co-illustrator is not of Latino heritage, the book is ineligible for consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The artist(s) or author(s) may be awarded the medal posthumously. One person may be selected to receive the awards in both categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of committee consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: The committee in its deliberations is to consider only the books eligible for the award, as specified in the terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The term “only the books eligible for the award” specifies that the committee is not to consider the entire body of work by an author or whether the author has previously won the award. The committee’s decision is to be made following deliberation about eligible books published in the preceding year. The committee should keep in mind that the award is for both literary/illustrative quality and presentation for children, as well as for its portrayal of the Latino cultural experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of “outstanding”
rubrics_metrics.description: “Outstanding” is defined as marked by eminence and distinction; noted for significant achievement; marked by excellence in quality; marked by conspicuous excellence or eminence; individually distinct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This definition frames the committee’s judgment of distinction and excellence across relevant elements of the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Textual criteria for judging authorship (children’s books)
rubrics_metrics.description: In identifying the author of an “outstanding” book for children, committee members need to consider: interpretation of the theme or concept; presentation of information including accuracy, clarity, and organization; development of a plot; delineation of characters; delineation of setting; appropriateness of style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because literary qualities vary depending on content, the committee need not expect excellence in each named element; the book should, however, have distinguished qualities in all elements pertinent. Excellence of presentation for an intended child audience is important. The committee is to make its decision primarily on the text; other aspects (e.g., illustrations, overall design) are to be considered only if they distract from the text. The book must be a self-contained entity, not dependent on other media (i.e., digital, sound or film equipment) for its enjoyment. Particular attention will be paid to cultural authenticity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illustration criteria for judging picture books
rubrics_metrics.description: In identifying the illustrator of an outstanding picture book for children, committee members need to consider: excellence of execution in the artistic technique employed; excellence of pictorial interpretation of story, theme, or concept; appropriateness of style of illustration to the story, theme or concept; delineation of plot, theme, characters, setting, mood or information through the pictures; positive and authentic portrayal of Latino culture; excellence of presentation for an intended child audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The only limitation to graphic form is that the form must be one which may be used in a picture book. The book must be a self-contained entity, not dependent on other media for its enjoyment. Each book is to be considered as a picture book and the committee is to make its decision primarily on the illustrations; other components (especially written text or overall design) are to be considered when they make a book less effective as a children’s picture book. Particular attention will be paid to cultural authenticity. The award is for both distinguished illustrations and for excellence of pictorial presentation for children and for the positive portrayal of the Latino cultural heritage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultural authenticity
rubrics_metrics.description: Particular attention will be paid to cultural authenticity in both textual and illustrative considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultural authenticity influences evaluation of portrayal, affirmation, and celebration of Latino cultural experience; it is mentioned repeatedly as a key focus for committee deliberations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-contained work requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The book must be a self-contained entity, not dependent on other media (i.e., digital, sound or film equipment) for its enjoyment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement applies to both text-focused and illustration-focused evaluations; dependence on other media may render a work less effective or ineligible for consideration as a picture or children’s book under these terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission procedural requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: How to submit books for consideration: complete the award submission for each entry; mail one copy of the work to the award committee chair and Cultural Competency Consultant; submit a Belpré Award Submission: Information Verification form for each book; deadline is December 31 of the publication year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review the terms and criteria and the committee manual for a comprehensive overview. ALSC membership is not required and there is no entry fee. The ALSC office requests one title mailed to the committee chair and the Cultural Competency Consultant; standards are in place for committee members to review and share submissions. Neither the ALSC office nor the committee chair can confirm receipt of submissions—use tracking if you want confirmation. Submissions dropped off in-person to the ALSC office will not be accepted. The ALSC office cannot answer eligibility questions or advise which award a submission is eligible for; eligibility is determined confidentially by the committee.
